# Motion · 动效

Recordings of motion in shipped products are the best teacher: watch them slowed down and note duration, easing, origin and what does not move. Then tools to author curves and springs, official guidelines, and the few writers worth reading.

57 resources, plus 5 cross-listed from other domains. Columns are explained in README.md; `python3 "$S/catalog.py" find` (`S` = `skills/design-studio/scripts`) searches every domain at once. Rows are sorted by tier, then by reach, so what an agent can fetch comes first.

## Motion in shipped products · 上线产品动效实录

Start here for any in-product animation.

| Resource | Best for | How to use | Tier | Kind | Reach | Access · licence | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [60fps.design](https://60fps.design) | Screen recordings of UI animation in shipped apps (mostly iOS), filterable by interaction pattern and app category; the best single source for mobile motion | Deep-link /shots/filter/<pattern> (loading, onboarding, navigation...) or /apps/category/<category>; play at 0.25-0.5x and write down duration, easing, origin and what stays still before specifying a transition | S | gallery | static | free | [Pattern filter (example: loading)](https://60fps.design/shots/filter/loading); [App category (example: finance)](https://60fps.design/apps/category/finance) |
| [Spotted in Prod](https://spottedinprod.com) | Short recordings of standout interaction details in shipped iOS apps, browsable by app and by style tag (minimal, skeuomorphic, playful, dense...) | Browse Apps or a style tag, open a clip and note trigger, duration and easing; it is iOS only, so translate the idiom before using it on Android or the web | S | gallery | static | free |  |
| [Ripplix](https://www.ripplix.com) | 7,000+ recorded UI animations from 1,000+ real apps and sites (mobile, web, watch, AR/VR), filterable by element (onboarding, success, dropdown, chart...) and industry | Start from All elements, pick the element you are designing and compare five products at reduced speed; note timing and what does not move | A | gallery | static | freemium | [All elements](https://www.ripplix.com/all-elements); [All apps and sites](https://www.ripplix.com/all-apps) |
| [Apple Design Awards](https://developer.apple.com/design/awards/) | Winners and finalists each year with video of the shipped app; the Interaction and Delight and Fun categories are a curated reel of platform-native motion | Watch the Interaction category videos frame by frame for gesture-driven, interruptible transitions; compare with Apple's HIG before copying an idiom | A | gallery | static | free |  |
| [Detail (multi)](https://detail.design) | Curated short recordings of the small decisions that make shipped software feel considered, tagged Design, Interactivity, Motion, Copywriting, Accessibility and Easter Egg | Filter to Motion or Interactivity and study one detail at a time: what triggers it, how long it runs and why it earns its place; a Chinese edition lives at /zh | A | gallery | static | freemium | [中文版 (Chinese edition)](https://detail.design/zh) |

## Easing, spring and animation tools · 曲线与弹簧工具

Author curves and springs by eye, then record the numbers as tokens.

| Resource | Best for | How to use | Tier | Kind | Reach | Access · licence | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Easing Wizard](https://easingwizard.com) | Generate and preview bezier, spring, bounce and wiggle easings, exported as CSS including linear() | Tune by eye with the preview, then copy the CSS | S | tool | static | free |  |
| [Easing Functions Cheat Sheet](https://easings.net) | Visual reference of the named easing functions with CSS and maths | Look up a named curve to copy its cubic-bezier; for product UI stay in the ease-out family (quart, quint, expo) and keep elastic and bounce for rare playful moments | A | tool | static | free |  |
| [CSS Spring Easing Generator](https://www.kvin.me/css-springs) | Turns a spring given as perceptual duration and bounce into a CSS linear() easing plus the matching real duration (--spring-easing and --spring-duration) | Enter the duration and bounce from the motion spec (the model SwiftUI and Motion use), copy both custom properties and always apply them together | A | tool | static | free |  |
| [Scroll-driven Animations](https://scroll-driven-animations.style) | Demos and visual tools for CSS scroll-driven animations (timeline ranges, view progress) | Use the range visualiser to pick animation-range values (entry, exit, cover, contain) and copy the CSS; test with prefers-reduced-motion on | A | tool | static | free |  |
| [View Transitions demos](https://view-transitions.chrome.dev) | Reference demos for same-document and cross-document view transitions | Copy the pattern closest to the navigation being designed | A | gallery | static | free |  |
| [Jitter](https://jitter.video) | Browser-based motion design tool with Lottie, video and GIF export | Import frames from Figma, animate on the timeline and export 4K video, GIF or Lottie; suited to marketing and brand motion rather than in-product UI | A | tool | static | freemium · login |  |
| [Rive](https://rive.app) | Editor and runtimes for interactive vector animation driven by state machines | Use when an animation must react to input across platforms; open marketplace files to study their state machines before building your own | A | tool | static | freemium · login | [Marketplace (remixable files, per-file licence)](https://rive.app/marketplace/) |
| [Lottie format docs](https://lottiefiles.github.io/lottie-docs/) | Readable reference of the Lottie JSON format (layers, shapes, keyframes, easing); the formal spec is now published by the Lottie Animation Community | Keep it open when generating or editing Lottie by code; check structure against the official spec linked here | A | spec | static | free · CC-BY-4.0 | [Official Lottie specification](https://lottie.github.io/lottie-spec/latest/) |
| [ProtoPie (multi)](https://www.protopie.io) | High-fidelity interaction prototyping without code: variables, conditions, device sensors and multi-screen links, playable on real devices | Prototype the one interaction whose feel is contested (a gesture, a sheet, a car HMI screen), test it on the device, then hand the timings to engineering | A | tool | static | freemium · login |  |
| [Chrome DevTools: Animations panel](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/animations) | Inspect, slow down (25% or 10%), scrub and edit the timing of CSS and Web Animations on any live page; the fastest way to measure a reference site's motion | Open a reference site, record in the Animations panel, replay at 10% and read durations, delays and easing; agents can do the same over CDP (Animation.setPlaybackRate) while capturing frames | A | tool | static | free | [CDP Animation domain (for scripted capture)](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Animation/) |

## Official motion guidance and accessibility · 官方动效指引与无障碍

Token tables, principles, and the rules for motion sensitivity.

| Resource | Best for | How to use | Tier | Kind | Reach | Access · licence | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [WWDC18: Designing Fluid Interfaces](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2018/803/) | The foundational talk on gesture-driven, interruptible, redirectable interfaces | Watch before designing any drag, sheet or swipe interaction | S | article | static | free · archived |  |
| [WWDC23: Animate with springs](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10158/) | Explains springs through duration and bounce instead of mass, stiffness and damping | Specify every spring as duration plus bounce; convert to mass, stiffness and damping only at implementation time, per platform | S | article | static | free |  |
| [Carbon motion](https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/motion/overview/) | IBM's two-mode motion system: productive (efficient, out of the way) versus expressive (for occasional important moments), with published cubic-bezier curves and six duration tokens from 70 ms to 700 ms | Copy the duration tokens (70, 110, 150, 240, 400, 700 ms) and the standard, entrance and exit curves of each mode as the skeleton of your own motion tokens | A | guideline | static | free |  |
| [NN/g: Animation duration](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/animation-duration/) | Evidence-based guidance on how long UI animations should last | Cite when pushing back on slow animation | A | article | static | free |  |
| [NN/g: Animation purpose](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/animation-purpose-ux/) | When motion helps: feedback, state change, navigation metaphors, signifiers | Use as the justification test for each animation | A | article | static | free |  |
| [WCAG: Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html) | The normative basis for letting users disable interaction-triggered motion | Read with 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide | A | spec | static | free | [Agent-readable mirror (w3c.github.io)](https://w3c.github.io/wcag/understanding/animation-from-interactions.html) |
| [web.dev: prefers-reduced-motion](https://web.dev/articles/prefers-reduced-motion) | How to implement reduced motion well on the web | Follow the no-motion-first pattern | A | article | static | free |  |
| [Designing Safer Web Animation For Motion Sensitivity](https://alistapart.com/article/designing-safer-web-animation-for-motion-sensitivity/) | Which kinds of motion trigger vestibular symptoms and how to design around them | Check parallax, zoom and large-area movement against it | A | article | static | free · archived |  |
| [Material 3 motion](https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview) | Motion system with easing and duration tokens, transition patterns and the expressive spring-based motion scheme | Read How it works for the standard and expressive spring schemes, then the tokens page for easing and duration values; record the numbers as tokens | A | guideline | js | free | [Easing and duration tokens](https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/easing-and-duration/tokens-specs) |
| [Material 2: Speed](https://m2.material.io/design/motion/speed.html) | Still the clearest public explanation of how duration and easing should vary with size, distance and platform | Read once; the reasoning outlives the version | A | guideline | js | free · archived |  |
| [Apple HIG: Motion](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion) | Apple's principles: purposeful, brief, optional motion; respecting Reduce Motion | Agents: fetch the page as JSON (…/human-interface-guidelines/motion.json) instead of the JS page; pair with the WWDC springs and fluid-interfaces talks | A | guideline | js | free | API `https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/{page}.json` |
| [HarmonyOS motion design principles (zh)](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/doc/design-guides/animation-design-principles-0000001750237392) | Huawei's motion principles for HarmonyOS apps with concrete duration caps: long moves within 350 ms, short within 250 ms, small within 150 ms | Use its six principles (natural, efficient, fast response, consistent, hide waiting, brand) and duration caps as the baseline for HarmonyOS targets | A | guideline | js | free |  |
| [Fluent 2 motion](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/motion) | Microsoft's motion principles and timing guidance | Read Duration and easing, then Choreography: give larger elements and longer distances more time, stagger lists with gaps that shorten as they go, and keep container transforms continuous | B | guideline | static | free |  |
| [Ant Motion (zh)](https://motion.ant.design) | Ant Design's motion language and React motion components | Read the three principles (natural, efficient, restrained) in the maintained Ant Design spec page; treat the Ant Motion React components as legacy | B | guideline | js | free · slow | [Ant Design 动效 spec (Markdown)](https://ant.design/docs/spec/motion-cn.md) |
